14.0.0.en: One of the rulers of the Pharisees invited Christ to a feast on the Sabbath day, not in order to honor Him but to catch Him in some error so as to cast doubt on Him among the people or stir up the authorities against Him. Christ accepted the invitation because He does not fear their schemes, and to seize the opportunity to do good or to teach them the truth; for He seeks the salvation of all. Do not be disturbed by the plots of those around you, for God protects you from them, and continue doing good and showing love to them for Christ's sake.

14.1.0.en: Jesus found before Him a man sick with dropsy, which is the retention of quantities of water in the body, so that it swells and does not benefit from drinking water, because the water does not reach its organs but is stored up to no purpose. Perhaps this man had heard of Christ's coming and came to be healed.

14.2.0.en: "The lawyers" are those concerned with applying the Law, and they were present in the house of the Pharisee ruler. Christ knew what was in the hearts of the Pharisees and the lawyers, their attempt to catch Him in some error, so He asked them whether it is lawful to heal on the Sabbath as a good work or not, to teach them that the Lord's day is a freeing from material works so that we may fill it with worship and doing good.

14.3.0.en: "He took him": to show His compassion and tenderness toward him.

14.3.1.en: "Let him go": so that he might return to his house and be kept away from the Pharisees' rebukes of him for being healed on the Sabbath day. The lawyers were unable to prove from the Law their wrong idea of not doing good on the Sabbath, so they were silent. And Christ was not hindered by their thoughts from doing good, so He took the sick man and healed him, then let him go enjoying health and freedom from the illness.

14.4.0.en: Christ confirmed to them the necessity of doing good on the Sabbath, by the proof that the Law provides that if someone's ox or ass falls into a pit, he will pull it out so that it does not die (Deut 22:4); how much more people, whom we should pity and help on the Sabbath day. And they were also unable to answer Him because of the strength of His argument.

14.5.0.en: The Pharisees felt that they were better than others, so they were eager to sit at the tables of feasts in the chief places at the head of the table. In order to treat this pride in all people, which He may have noticed at the supper of this Pharisee who hosted Him, He told the following example.

14.6.0.en: If you are invited to a wedding feast, do not sit in the places of honor, lest the master of the wedding come and ask you to leave this place because a person of better standing has come after you, and you are ashamed and leave the place and go to a less honorable one. For if a person thinks he is better than others, the Lord will bring the humble and put them in heaven in his place, while he goes far away, contrary to what he supposed.

14.7.0.en: Christ advised His hearers that a person should seek the lowest room in humility, feeling that he is less than others, and because Christ humbled Himself by His incarnation and His death on the cross. If you take the lower place, you find Christ beside you, that is, you feel His presence with you and He fills your heart. But if the master of the wedding calls you to a better place, thank him; there is no objection to taking the better place, and you receive it as a grace from God that you do not deserve. Of course, do not take the last place with the aim that the host will honor you before everyone, so that your humility is seen and you become puffed up with pride in the virtue of humility, for this is hypocrisy and false humility.

14.7.1.en: And the host's bringing you forward to a better place means that God honors you and glorifies you before all creation on the day of judgment.

14.8.0.en: Christ declared the truth plainly, that the proud one who exalts himself is brought low by God, but whoever seeks humility, God exalts him and honors him.

14.8.1.en: Humility and hiddenness in your dealings with others are not a giving up of a better place, but a spiritual wisdom, because, away from the outward greatness before people, you experience Christ and feel His presence with you. By your humility you are the wisest of people, because you are seeking the most important thing, which is the companionship of God, given only to the humble. And do not be distressed if people neglect you and you feel alone and isolated, but seek God and seize this opportunity for more prayers and readings, and God will reveal Himself to you and you will rejoice in Him with a joy that cannot be expressed.

14.9.0.en: Christ directed His words to those who give feasts, that they should not invite their great friends so as to be repaid with similar feasts in their houses; in this way feasts become a business, for they take in return for what they give, and there is no giving in them to the needy. Nor should feasts be an occasion for boasting of the abundance of food and the arrangements of the feast; whoever does this also receives his reward, which is the praise of people, and he has no reward with God.

14.9.1.en: But this does not mean that love feasts for relatives and friends are rejected, if their purpose is love and fellowship and the sense of God's presence in their midst.

14.10.0.en: "The maimed": those whose noses or one of their limbs have been cut off, so they are disfigured and hindered from ordinary work, and therefore poor.

14.10.1.en: "The resurrection of the just": that is, the last day, when the righteous are rewarded in the Kingdom of Heaven, and the wicked are cast into eternal torment.

14.10.2.en: Christ advised inviting the poor, whether the weak and disfigured (the maimed) or the lame and the blind, and everyone who appears poor or of lower standing in society, for these are unable to make similar feasts, and in this way your feast is love without return, and God repays you for it with the heavenly reward, that is, He honors you and hosts you in the Kingdom of Heaven.

14.10.3.en: Be concerned with giving without return, that is, do not hope for repayment from all those around you, for the heavenly reward is better than every earthly return. And serve not only those who are poor materially, but rather the weak and disfigured spiritually by the multitude of sins, the lame who cannot walk in the way of the Kingdom, and the blind who do not see God because of their absorption in the desires of the world.

14.11.s.en: (4) The supper and the invited guests

14.11.0.en: It seems that one of the Pharisees or Jews rejoiced at Christ's words about the heavenly reward for whoever invites the poor, so he praised whoever eats bread in the Kingdom of Heaven, because his idea of heaven was material, as he thought that there is eating and drinking there as in the world.

14.12.0.en: "Bade": accepting the invitation is preparing for life with God, not the life itself, as shown by the fact that many accepted the invitation but at the time of fulfillment refused for many reasons, as happens today, when many declare their faith in theory but at the practical application in worshipping God and loving others they make excuses for different reasons.

14.12.1.en: On this occasion Christ gave a parable about preparing for the heavenly Kingdom: a certain man made a great supper, and bade many.

14.12.2.en: This man signifies God, who made a supper by His death on the cross, and the offering of His Body and Blood on the altar every day in the Church, which is the pledge of the spiritual heavenly feast that He gives to His children in heaven. And He bade many, for He died for the redemption of the whole world, for He is the one "who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4).

14.13.0.en: "His servant": that is, Christ, who took the form of a servant by His incarnation, and came to call people to the feast of His most holy Body and Blood, which He accomplishes on the cross. The servant also signifies the Apostles, who call people to the Church and to preparing for the Kingdom.

14.13.1.en: "For all things are now ready": the Church is open and in it are the Body and Blood of the Lord, and it awaits the believers to be united with Him.

14.14.0.en: "All" means most of those invited first, who are the Jews, the people of God.

14.14.1.en: "With one consent": they agreed to neglect faith in Christ, being occupied with material things and honor.

14.14.2.en: Five yoke of oxen signify the five senses, that is, the desires of the senses.

14.14.3.en: When the invited were called they excused themselves from coming; God calls us to repentance many times and we refuse. The excuses were very foolish: the first excused himself because he had bought a piece of ground and wanted to see it, although examining fields is not done at night at suppertime.

14.14.4.en: And this first one signifies those absorbed in earthly things and the love of possessions.

14.14.5.en: The second excused himself because he had bought five yoke of oxen and wanted to prove them. This also is not done at suppertime but in the daytime, and he signifies those occupied with bodily desires.

14.14.6.en: The third excused himself because of his marriage. He signifies those occupied with the world and its ties.

14.14.7.en: And these three point to those of the Jews who refuse God, because God called them first and they refused, and then He called the Gentiles afterward.

14.14.8.en: Examine the excuses you tell yourself to justify your keeping away from the Church, prayers and service, lest they be foolish and make you lose the Kingdom.

14.15.0.en: God, the master of the supper, was angry at the refusal of the Pharisees, the priests and the rulers of the Jews to accept His invitation to salvation, and He sent to call the common Jews, the poor and simple, and likewise the Gentiles, to His Kingdom, and gathered them from their lowly places in the streets and lanes to raise them by His love to heaven.

14.16.0.en: The servants, that is, the Apostles, did as God commanded them, and many of the simple Jews and the Gentiles came into the faith, so the Apostles told God all about their service and that there is still room in the Kingdom, that is, the blood of Christ is offered for the salvation of all if they believe.

14.17.0.en: "The highways and hedges" are places outside the cities and signify the distant Gentiles.

14.17.1.en: "That my house may be filled": because God rejoices to receive all believers in His Kingdom.

14.17.2.en: "None of those men which were bidden": none of those men invited earlier at the beginning of the parable who refused to come to the supper, that is, life with God on earth; these have no place in the Kingdom of Heaven.

14.17.3.en: God sent His servants a second time to "compel" the poor who are far from God, that is, to encourage them and support them strongly, since from the extremity of their weakness they have fallen into despair and need support; for He seeks the salvation of all the distant ones who do not know the way to the Kingdom, but as for those who know and refuse, God affirms that He will not bring them into His Kingdom. God has pity on the weak and sinners, seeks them and supports them and urges them on in the way of the Kingdom, but He hates stubbornness, recklessness and making light of sin.

14.18.0.en: "Great multitudes went with him": Christ was on His way from Galilee to Jerusalem, and the people of the cities and villages came out to Him and followed Him to hear His teachings and to be healed of their diseases.

14.18.1.en: In order to resist superficiality in the lives of His followers, Christ set conditions for salvation and asked us to examine ourselves by them, for they are the cost of obtaining salvation. Although salvation is free by the blood of Christ, He gives it only to those who strive spiritually. The first condition in spiritual striving is that we love God with all the heart, and love our relatives and dear ones whom God has given us, but if our love for anyone or for ourselves hinders us from God, let us hate it and reject it. So we love people and ourselves through God and for the sake of God who gave them to us.

14.19.0.en: The second condition in spiritual striving is bearing the cross, that is, enduring suffering for holding fast to the faith, and likewise the striving of spiritual worship and service, and in this we become Christ's disciples.

14.20.0.en: Christ gave an example of counting the cost: a man who wants to build a tower reckons whether he has the cost of building, lest he lay the foundation and be unable to finish the building, and people mock him because he wasted his money in vain and reached nothing.

14.20.1.en: The spiritual person who wants to build a tower, that is, a spiritual relationship that ties him to heaven, must lay the foundation, which is faith in Christ, and be ready to strive in prayers and fasts, in holding to the commandments, and in repentance with contrition; then the demons, his enemies, will not mock him.

14.20.2.en: So whoever wants to follow Christ asks himself whether he is ready not to be occupied with love of himself and attachment to others, and likewise whether he is ready for detachment and for enduring suffering for the sake of the faith!

14.20.3.en: If so, let him go forward with confidence in the spiritual life; but whoever is moved by Christ's words while his heart is attached to the love of the world and to emotional attachments that distract him from God will not be able to complete his way with God. Christ's call to count the cost is not to frighten His followers with the difficulty of the way, but to urge them to prepare by making Him their only goal and being bound to His love, so that they are assured of reaching the Kingdom and enjoying His ever-joyful companionship.

14.21.0.en: The other parable on counting the cost is of a king who has an army of ten thousand soldiers and is going to fight another whose force is twenty thousand soldiers; he should first think whether he has the means to win or make peace, so as not to be exposed to defeat and death. The meaning is that this warring king should examine his strength: is he able to face the enemy's army? Likewise whoever wants to walk with God should examine his readiness to leave his attachment to material things and to people for God's sake, so that he succeeds in overcoming all his desires and the adverse circumstances of life, and thus is assured of reaching the Kingdom.

14.21.1.en: The warring king with ten thousand soldiers signifies the spiritual person; the number ten points to the commandments, and the thousand to heaven. The spiritual person fights with God's commandments and with attachment to eternity, but the enemy, Satan, fights with twenty, a war divided into two parts: the first part, signified by ten, a complete war, consists of the blows on the right, which are exaggeration in worship and good works for the purpose of pride; and the second part, signified by the second ten, also a complete war, consists of the blows on the left, which are all kinds of sins and desires.

14.21.2.en: If a person feels that he is weak, he must be reconciled with God so that God may be his strength and he may overcome the demons; he sends the intercession of the saints, that is, the embassy, and repents of his sins and so makes peace with God.

14.21.3.en: It is also possible for the warring king with ten thousand to signify the spirit, and the enemy king who has twenty thousand to signify the body, so the person examines himself: is the spirit strong and able to overcome the body and lead it in the way of the spiritual life? Otherwise he sends an embassy, that is, consults a father of confession, and is reconciled with his body by taking lighter spiritual exercises that the body can bear, then gradually grows in his striving and spiritual exercises, with the spirit and body in agreement and at peace in the way of the Kingdom.

14.22.0.en: Christ lays down the third condition in spiritual striving, which is relying on God and not on the wealth of the world, so the spiritual person detaches himself from it and gives it to the needy, and is not disturbed if he loses some of it.

14.23.0.en: "Ears": the meaning is to hear with both ears, that is, with full attention; it also means by the two ears the outer ear and the inner ear in the heart, that is, spiritual understanding, and it means hearing His word, understanding it and applying it in life.

14.23.1.en: Salt keeps food from corruption and gives it a good taste; likewise the children of God are responsible for declaring the truth, doing good and keeping God's commandments. But if the salt (the children of God) loses its savor by mixing with the world and desires and by refusing to bear the cross and every spiritual striving, it will lose its saltiness and all its qualities, and then it is of no use and is cast into eternal torment; that is, the children of God who have abandoned their spiritual life and become absorbed in the world are condemned, and their judgment is harder.

14.23.2.en: If God has revealed to us the conditions of salvation, we must strive in them, confident of His love which upholds us and gives us the Kingdom.

14.23.3.en: The parables of the lost sheep, the lost coin and the prodigal son. The parable of the lost sheep (vv. 1-7):

14.23.5.en: 1- Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him. 2- And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, "This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them." 3- And he spake this parable unto them, saying, 4- What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? 5- And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing. 6- And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost. 7- I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
